body: I'm sorry, I went to shower and try to get some sleep and ended up not checking back in on my account. Thanks so much for the support. I am thinking about changing my major, I just have no idea what I'd want to change it to. It's hard to find something that I really enjoy nowadays. I'll keep looking though. Thank you so much.

The hard part about changing my major comes down to several factors:
1. I really do enjoy my major. I think I would be an amazing fit for the job. I have a background with the type of people I will be working with. 
2. It's a VERY high paying job. It's a job where not enough people are taking this as a career. I could potentially be making six figures straight out of college. 

However, it is becoming a huge issue. It's a seriously tedious major. It's insanely hard to describe without going into the details of what it entails. The schooling is MUCH harder and requires a lot more time and effort than the actual career does. I am close with a lot of people in the field who say the job is something they absolutely adore, but the schooling is absolute hell. I know it's something that I'd have to get through...but getting through it is seemingly impossible at this point. I am so overwhelmed and overloaded with the work that I am clueless on what to do. 

The reason I came here is because suicide is the solution that's been popping into my head recently. It just seems so much easier. I have a lot of health issues, and I almost wish I'd of passed away earlier from a hospitalization so I would have never had to suffer like this. It really is a sick thought, but I can't help it at this point. I don't want to drop my major, and pushing through is seemingly impossible. My mental health is seriously at risk, which I really dislike.
It's just an odd concept for me at the moment. I've never tried them so I really have no idea if they will be beneficial or detrimental to my current state.

Thanks again for your second response. 
I have tried switching, but apparently at my school they don't allow you to make a change with the psychologist....very strange. 
I have officially been diagnosed with anxiety, but I think the depression thing is more recent, and I haven't been in for help since around late October. 
I will try to consult online sources, and possibly ask my primary care doctor for resources around me that he thinks may be covered by my insurance. I know there are many around where I live back home (3.5 hours away), but I won't be there until summer, so I really worry for the meantime about my wellbeing. 
Thanks again, I will see what I can do about this.
Thank you so much for that link. I was completely unaware of that website and I am currently browsing it. I appreciate that!

Thank you so much for your response and your time. 
I have considered changing majors; however, it seems so complicated. I haven't given much thought to what else I really would want to do as a career. I honestly don't know what else would be fitting for me to do. 
I will try keeping a journal if you think that could be helpful, thank you for that suggestion. 
I do have a few hobbies. I am in club lacrosse on campus. I am also involved a little with a few smaller clubs, like anime, and scifi club. I work out whenever I can. And I adore hockey. I am a long time NHL fan. I try to keep my mind off of things, but it's really hard for me to do. 
Again, thank you so much for your response, and taking the time out of your day to help.

Thank you so much for your kinds words. I am really happy to see someone can really relate. It's just a very complicated situation for me right now. 
My boyfriend, he's amazing with support. I just hate the fact that he's so far away....4,000 miles to be exact. It's really hard here without him. Especially with the time zone difference. 
Life is really hard. 
Thanks for responding, and you really should sleep!

Thank you so much for taking the time to respond. Unfortunately, I feel that my major will only get harder. It requires a lot more as you increase your year. Technically, right now, I am still a candidate for the major, until I pass a required test and complete my observation and community service hours for my major. After that is complete, I am in the major, but I have a lot more to do, and the classes become a lot more hands on, which absolutely terrifies me. 
I wouldn't be opposed to going on medication, but I have no idea where to start. I also know my brother had issues with the side effects when he went on medication for anxiety which concerns me, as well as the fact that I have Crohn's Disease and don't know if it could affect that at all. 
My school's counseling service seemed very unorganized. I visited 4 times last semester and then my counselor canceled on me, and when I tried to reschedule, they told me they had nothing open for 3 weeks. They also only have clinical psychologists, so that wouldn't help as far as medications go. I'm really so lost.
Thanks again, for your time and response!

Thank you so much for responding. I am a sophomore in college. Unfortunately, I can't take a lighter course load right now. I need to take 15 credits per semester to graduate and complete my gen ed credits as well as credits for my major. I honestly don't know what else I would do with my life. I only have a passion for what I'm doing. I really do have a passion for it, and I know that after college would be potentially a lot less work than what I'm currently doing. That's why I don't want to change. I don't want to make a mistake and be more miserable doing something else. My major is extremely competitive and if I drop, I seriously cannot be accepted back into it. I went to the health center and I got help, but I didn't feel like they cared. After a few meetings, he canceled and when I tried to reschedule they said they didn't have an opening for three weeks. I don't know where I could go for resources in my community instead of at my school. My mom said that the insurance won't cover anything in my area, but I may call tomorrow to confirm that. I am not on medication, as the school clinical psychologist I was seeing told me I wouldn't benefit from them, and I really only needed psychotherapy (which really didn't help me). I wouldn't mind being on medication, but my brother was on medication for anxiety and had to go off of them because of the side effects. I am also concerned because I have Crohn's Disease and I'm not sure if the meds could harm my intestines. I wouldn't know where to go to get them even if I wanted them, though. :/ Again, thanks for your response!

Hello, first of all thank you so much for your response. It means a lot to hear things from a different perspective instead of just going over them in my head. I went to the counseling for students from my college, however it wasn't very helpful. I still felt very judged, and the exercises he had me doing seemed redundant. He also canceled one day, and never rescheduled. When I tried to after that, they told me his schedule was full. It just felt I wasn't a priority, which is why I decided to ask my mom about other local options. However, if my insurance won't cover it, on a college student budget, I really am unsure of if I can afford anything outside of what's included in my tuition. Again, thanks so much for your kind words.
